html:
The Wet'suwet'en are a First Nation of the Bulkley River valley in northern British Columbia. Yintikh means their land. They speak an Athabaskan language, Babine-Witsuwit'en.

They fished for salmon in the Bulkley River canyons, hunted and trapped. From their western neighbours the Gitxsan they share a system of clans and house groups, with hereditary chiefs who hold the land and confirm their rights at feasts.

With the Gitxsan they went to court for their land in the case Delgamuukw v. British Columbia, decided by the Supreme Court of Canada in 1997. In 2019 and 2020 hereditary chiefs opposed a gas pipeline across their territory, and protests in support blocked railways across Canada. Neighbours to the east include the Nadleh Whut'en.
sum: The Wet'suwet'en are a First Nation of the Bulkley River valley in northern British Columbia. Yintikh means their land. They speak an Athabaskan language, Babine-Witsuwit'en.
